tagline: Iron Range to North Shore, and no towns between.
intro: Out of the Iron Range at Aurora and Hoyt Lakes, two-lane county roads head southeast through the Superior National Forest to Silver Bay on Lake Superior. There are no towns along the way, only north woods, lakes, creeks and marshes, with hardwoods among the pines that turn red and yellow in the fall.

Both ends of the road were built for taconite. Hoyt Lakes was laid out in 1955 to serve a mine that worked from 1956 to 2008, and Silver Bay began in 1954 as a company town processing ore sent down by train from Babbitt.

moments.title: Skibo Vista
moments.text: The overlook that gave Skibo Lookout Road its name looks out over the Laurentian Divide, and in migration season hawks can be watched passing over it.

moments.title: Toimi School
moments.text: Finnish settlers built this schoolhouse in 1913, and children who spoke Finnish at home had to speak English once they came through its doors, until it closed in 1942.

moments.title: Silver Bay
moments.text: At the end of the road the taconite town keeps Black Beach, rich in taconite tailings and opened to the public in 2015.
